images.title: Rectangle diagonal does not fold
images.purpose: Show that the diagonal of a rectangle that is not a square cuts two equal pieces that do not overlap when folded.
images.composition: A rectangle and a square side by side with wide space between them, each with a diagonal.
images.exact_structure: Left: one rectangle 6 cm long and 3 cm wide, filled teal #0072B2, corners lettered A, B, C, D going round, with one dashed diagonal from A (top left) to C (bottom right), and one cross beside it. Right: one square 4 cm by 4 cm, filled amber #E69F00, with one dashed diagonal from top left to bottom right, and one tick beside it. Exactly 2 shapes, 2 diagonals, 1 cross, 1 tick.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a rectangle drawn as a square, or a rectangle diagonal drawn as a line of symmetry
images.takeaway: Two equal pieces are not enough; the halves must overlap.
images.description: A teal rectangle 6 cm by 3 cm with corners A to D and a dashed diagonal that does not fold onto itself, next to an amber square with its diagonal that does.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why the square diagonal folds exactly but the rectangle diagonal leaves overhangs.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
